segments.note: The Boston & Worcester RR (opened 1835) and the Western RR (Worcester-Springfield 1837-39, Springfield-state line 1841) completed a through Boston-Albany rail connection in 1841 via the connecting Albany & West Stockbridge RR - the first rail link between Boston and the Hudson/Erie Canal system. Still separate companies at this point; frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The Boston & Worcester and Western railroads merged in 1867 to form the Boston and Albany Railroad; the Albany & West Stockbridge and Hudson & Boston railroads joined in Dec 1870, unifying the route under one company. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The New York Central and Hudson River Railroad leased the B&A for 99 years starting July 1, 1900, operating it as the NYC's Boston & Albany Division. Boston-section trains (New England States and others) joined/split from NYC's Chicago trains at Albany (see new_york_central.geojson for that connecting history). Service wound down through the mid-20th century like the rest of the NYC system; Amtrak took over May 1, 1971. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
